from.place: Proof input for the affine closed-immersion restriction: identify the induced inverse image with sheafification of evaluation along the lift, and evaluate it on weakly contractible basis objects.

title: Affine closed immersion inverse-image evaluation
statement: Let $i:Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\hookrightarrow X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be a closed immersion of affine schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-scheme]. Write $X_{\mathrm{app}}=\mathcal B_X$ and $Z_{\mathrm{app}}=\mathcal B_Z$ for the affine ind-etale bases [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] of their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and use the functors $u,v$ of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-site-functor-properties]. Let $i^{-1}$ be the inverse image for the ordinary base-change morphism of topoi [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and write $R_Z$ for restriction of sheaves to $Z_{\mathrm{app}}$. For every sheaf of sets $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $R_Z(i^{-1}F)$ is naturally isomorphic to the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] on $Z_{\mathrm{app}}$ of the presheaf $V\mapsto F(v(V))$. If $V$ is weakly contractible in $Z_{\mathrm{app}}$, then $(i^{-1}F)(V)\cong F(v(V))$, naturally in $F$ and such $V$. Here weakly contractible in a site means that every epimorphism $P\to Q$ of sheaves of sets on that site induces a surjection $P(V)\to Q(V)$; an epimorphism means a right-cancellable morphism.

proof.text: Work in the small sites and universes of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For each affine scheme $S=X,Z$, [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] supplies cover-density of the full inclusion $\mathcal B_S\subset S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and finite basis refinements of coverings. Its topology is induced by this inclusion by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]: a covering sieve in the full site has a basis refinement, and a basis cover is a full-site cover. Thus [lem-pc-fppf-dense-sheaf-equivalence], with values in sets (small structured-arrow limits exist as sets of compatible families), makes restriction $R_S$ an equivalence of sheaf categories. If $H$ is a sheaf on $Z_{\mathrm{proet}}$, [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] gives $(R_Xi_*H)(U)=H(U\times_X Z)=(R_ZH)(u(U))$. Consequently the ordinary direct image is represented on these bases by precomposition with $u$.

source.place: Tag 09BL, lemma-closed-immersion-affines-apply, opening paragraph; Tag 098X, lemma-affine-alternative

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-site-functor-properties], $u$ is continuous and $v\dashv u$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] to $u$ and sets. Its left adjoint is $F\mapsto(u_pR_XF)^\#$, with $u_pR_XF(V)=\operatorname{colim}_{(U,\phi:V\to u(U))^{\mathrm{op}}}F(U)$. Let $\eta: \mathrm{id}\to uv$ be the unit. Under the adjunction, each $\phi$ corresponds to a unique $a:v(V)\to U$ with $u(a)\eta_V=\phi$. The pair $(v(V),\eta_V)$ is initial before taking the opposite. Explicitly the map on the colimit sends the class of $s\in F(U)$ to $F(a)(s)\in F(v(V))$; its inverse sends $t\in F(v(V))$ to its class at $(v(V),\eta_V)$. The colimit relation for $a$ makes these inverse, and uniqueness of $a$ makes the formula compatible with all transitions. Naturality of the adjunction gives compatibility with arrows $V'\to V$ and with maps $F\to F'$. This identifies $u_pR_XF$ with $G_F(V)=F(v(V))$. Both $R_Zi^{-1}F$ and $G_F^\#$ represent the same functor $H\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(R_XF,H\circ u)$ on basis sheaves, by step 1 and the two adjunctions. The natural-Hom criterion [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] identifies them canonically, naturally in $F$. This proves the first clause without asserting that $v$ preserves fibre products.

proof.text: For any covering $\{V_j\to V\}$ of $\mathcal B_Z$, its image $\{v(V_j)\to v(V)\}$ is a covering by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-site-functor-properties]. Since $F$ is a sheaf, two sections of $F(v(V))$ agreeing after these restrictions are equal. Thus $G_F$ is separated. The local-equality assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] now shows that the canonical map $\theta:G_F\to G_F^\#$ is injective on every object: equality of images gives equality on some cover, and separatedness gives equality before restricting.

source.place: Tag 09BL, proof of (2), separatedness paragraph; Sites Tag 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification

proof.text: Finite disjoint unions remain in $\mathcal B_Z$ and $\mathcal B_X$. Indeed, present the finitely many coordinate algebras $B_j$ as filtered colimits of etale finite-presentation algebras $B_{j,\alpha_j}$, using [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. The finite product of the indexing categories is filtered: choose an object in each coordinate for nonemptiness, a common upper object in each coordinate for two tuples, and a coordinatewise equalizer for parallel arrows. For each coordinate, forgetting the unused indices does not change its colimit: every representative can be completed by choosing unused indices, and common upper objects in those indices identify all choices. On this product indexing category the map $\operatorname{colim}_{(\alpha_j)}\prod_jB_{j,\alpha_j}\to\prod_jB_j$ is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] for sets. The filtered set colimits are the underlying sets of the algebra colimits: addition and multiplication are computed after moving finitely many representatives to a common index, and the algebra axioms and universal property follow at that index. Hence the displayed bijection respects all ring operations coordinatewise. Each stage is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-product] and finitely presented directly: take finite generators and relations for each coordinate, adjoin orthogonal idempotents $e_j$ with $\sum_j e_j=1$, impose $e_jx=x$ on every generator of coordinate $j$, and multiply each coordinate relation by $e_j$. These finitely many relations present the product, since its $e_j$-summand has precisely the given presentation of $B_{j,\alpha_j}$. This is an ind-etale presentation of the product; for the empty product the zero ring is already etale by the same cited node. The disjoint-union scheme is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry], and its coordinate ring is this product (sections of a sheaf on finitely many disjoint open components are the product of their sections). The coproduct property holds in each basis since it is a full subcategory. For $W=\coprod_jV_j$ and every $U\in\mathcal B_X$, the adjunction in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-site-functor-properties] gives $\operatorname{Hom}(v(W),U)=\operatorname{Hom}(W,u(U))=\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}(V_j,u(U))=\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}(v(V_j),U)$. These bijections identify the arrows $v(V_j)\to v(W)$ with coprojections, so $v(W)$ is canonically the finite disjoint union of the $v(V_j)$. Apply the sheaf evaluation clause of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry] to $F$: $G_F(W)=F(v(W))\cong\prod_jF(v(V_j))=\prod_jG_F(V_j)$. For an empty family both values are singletons.

source.place: Tag 09BL, proof of (2), finite disjoint-union paragraph

proof.text: Let $V$ be weakly contractible in $\mathcal B_Z$. Every cover of $V$ can be refined by a finite basis cover by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]; for such a cover $\{V_j\to V\}$ form $q:W=\coprod_jV_j\to V$. The arrow $q$ is ind-etale, hence weakly etale, by the relative-map clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], since its source and target are basis objects. This singleton is a cover: the original finite family is jointly surjective, and composing its component maps with the open-and-closed inclusions into $W$ gives the same image; for any affine open $O\subset V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, choose finitely many principal opens $D(f_a)$ of $V$ contained in $O$ and covering it (principal opens are a basis and $O$ is quasi-compact). Their inverse images in the affine scheme $W$ are the affine principal opens $D(q^*f_a)$ and their images cover $O$ by surjectivity of $q$. The pro-etale covering criterion is [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The representables $h_W,h_V$ are sheaves on the basis: they are restrictions of full-site representable sheaves by the subcanonical clause of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry]. The arrow $h_q:h_W\to h_V$ is an epimorphism. To check right cancellation, maps $h_V\to T$ correspond to sections $T(V)$ by [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection]; equality after $h_q$ is equality after restriction to $W$, hence equality by the sheaf condition for the singleton cover. The assumed surjectivity of evaluation at $V$ on epimorphisms of basis sheaves therefore makes $h_W(V)\to h_V(V)$ surjective. A preimage of $\mathrm{id}_V$ is a scheme arrow $\sigma:V\to W$ with $q\sigma=\mathrm{id}_V$. This proves the needed cover splitting directly, including the empty cover when $V$ is empty.

proof.text: Given $s\in G_F^\#(V)$, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] gives a cover on which $s$ is the image of sections of $G_F$. Refine it to a finite basis cover $\{V_j\to V\}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis], restricting the chosen sections to obtain $t_j\in G_F(V_j)$. The product bijection of step 4 gives $t\in G_F(W)$ with restrictions $t_j$. The two sections $\theta_W(t)$ and $s|_W$ of the sheaf $G_F^\#$ agree on the component cover $\{V_j\to W\}$, so they are equal. Pull back along the section $\sigma:V\to W$ of step 5. Naturality of $\theta$ gives $\theta_V(G_F(\sigma)t)=G_F^\#(\sigma)(s|_W)=s$, because $q\sigma=\mathrm{id}_V$. Thus $\theta_V$ is surjective, and it is injective by step 3. Together with step 2 this yields $(i^{-1}F)(V)\cong F(v(V))$. These isomorphisms are the inverses of the canonical evaluation maps $\theta_V$ followed by the canonical identification in step 2; they therefore commute with maps of sheaves and with restrictions between weakly contractible basis objects. No choices of cover or section enter the resulting isomorphism.

split_report.summary: Proved the two clauses of Stacks 09BL on the ind-etale bases: transported the ordinary direct image through dense-subsite restriction, evaluated its left Kan extension using v adjoint to u, and proved that sheafification does not change evaluation at a weakly contractible basis object. Wrote out finite disjoint unions, covering-representable epimorphisms and singleton-cover sections. No new nodes or statement changes.
